speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are presenting with dizziness, nausea, and an imbalance. To help me understand the root cause, how did you first notice these symptoms and how long have they been going on?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The patient's history of "room spinning" since this morning, exacerbated by garlic intake (which can irritate the inner ear) and relieved by diphenhydramine, along with a lack of other neurological deficits, is most consistent with BPPV. I am confident in this diagnosis and will proceed to treat accordingly.
